runs.name: REAX 1.3
runs.note: REAX's released REAX 1.3 weights (decisionmodels/REAX-1.3 at fa4bf7e), a decision model of two parts that both score every question; each option's probability is the 50/50 mean of the two parts'. Part G blends CharlieBT/gx31-decider (Gemma line, from tattrongvu/Jeffan-31b-1710) with PelaAI/KnowLine-31B-Gen1 (Gemma-4-31B); part Q blends gurujustin/sn92-gen-p5 (Qwen3.5-27B line, through baselabs/mammoth-1) with vllm-sr/d3-ultra. The model card calls REAX a decentralised lab on Bittensor subnet 92. It ran on our hardware through the maker's engine (the reax13 mode of reaxlabs/reax-engine at ff8f595, its own server, serve.py), both parts in FP8 (block-128) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, text only, one request at a time. Its card lists English only.

runs.note: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

coverage.definitions: All series are counted on the same kept reading questions; a full-bank run is restricted to them; first runs only. Answered = right + wrong (an invalid answer or one without a score is never answered). Coverage = answered / kept questions. Risk = error rate among answered = wrong / answered. Abstained: for a native point, the times the model chose the option; for a curve point, kept questions - answered - invalid. A native point is the run with its abstention option (Turkish "Bilmiyorum", Turkish "I don't know" as the wording control, English "I don't know"); Turkish "Bilmiyorum" is the Turkish side of the English "I don't know" comparison or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run; a missing one reads Not run (Running while a chat model's run is still going). A curve is one five-option run held back by its recorded score (the probability of the chosen option): one point per distinct score s, answering when the score is at least s; answers with equal scores enter together, so coverage moves in jumps and every point is an achieved one; all distinct points kept, ordered by coverage.

dont_know_same_answers.rule: Each model's five-option run (Turkish: every main run on the Text tab, all its setups, each its own Text tab run; English: its first English run) keeps exactly k answers, k being the reference's answered count (right + wrong) in its run with "I don't know"; a run with fewer than k scored answers keeps none: wrong, wrong_of_answers, difference, interval, p and p_holm stay null, its curve still has its points, and it is left out of the bootstrap and of Holm's correction (the reference having fewer than k stops the export). A run's scored answers (score and choice not null; any other answer is never kept) are ranked by score, highest first, equal scores by question id ascending (answers.json questions.id), never by correctness; the first k are kept, and wrong is the number of wrong answers among them, a whole number. wrong_of_answers = wrong / k; difference = a model's wrong_of_answers - the reference's. A curve has one point [answered, wrong] per k from 1 to the run's scored answers, under the same selection. Paired bootstrap over questions: per family a new random.Random(20261103), Turkish first, English second; 10,000 resamples, each rng.choices(range(n), k=n) over the family's n question positions in answers.json order, each question counting as often as it was drawn (k stays fixed). In a resample the answers are ordered by (score descending, question id ascending), the copies of a question together, and the first k copies are kept, only as many copies of the boundary question as k needs: wrong = the wrong copies before the boundary question + (k - the copies before it) * (1 if it is wrong, else 0). d = a model's wrong / k - the reference's. Two-sided p = min(1, 2 * min(1 + #{d <= 0}, 1 + #{d >= 0}) / 10,001); the 95% interval is the percentile interval, the 250th smallest and the 250th largest of the 10,000 resampled d. Holm's correction within each family over the models other than the reference that keep k answers (Turkish: the other main runs; English: the other English reading models), in the family's order.

high_confidence.rule: An answer counts when its chosen option has probability at least the cutoff; an answer without a score or without a valid choice never counts; wrong is a counted answer that is not right.
